atAGlance: Bánh căn is small griddled rice cakes, usually with quail egg or seafood, herbs, and nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili.
whatItIs: Bánh căn are small south-central rice pancakes cooked in clay molds, often with quail egg, seafood, scallions, and nước chấm. They are softer and more custardy than bánh khọt.
howToEnjoy: Dip the small cakes into nước chấm while they are warm, adding herbs and pickles if served. Ask about egg or seafood before ordering if either matters.
howLocalsOrder: Order bánh căn by portion size and topping. Ask for no chili in the nước chấm or a seafood-free version before the cakes go into the molds.
worthKnowing: Bánh căn is a south-central snack, especially around Đà Lạt, Nha Trang, and Phan Rang, where tiny clay-mold pancakes become a whole meal of dips and herbs.
goodToKnow: Quail egg, shrimp, or pork may be cooked into the little cakes; ask before ordering if you need a plain or vegetarian set.
